items.question: Which is the odd one out: Apple, Mango, Carrot, Banana?
items.explanation: Step 1: Find what most of them have in common. Step 2: Apple, mango and banana are fruits. Step 3: A carrot is a root vegetable, so it is the odd one out.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.question: If CAT is written as DBU (each letter moves one step forward), then DOG is written as EPH.
items.explanation: Step 1: In the code, C→D, A→B, T→U: each letter moves one step forward. Step 2: Do the same for DOG: D→E, O→P, G→H. Step 3: DOG becomes EPH.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.question: If 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C and so on, what does 8-5-12-16 spell?
items.explanation: Step 1: Count letters of the alphabet: 8 = H, 5 = E. Step 2: 12 = L, 16 = P. Step 3: Put them together: HELP. (HELM would end in 13 = M.)
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.fact: A mirror swaps left and right. That is why the word AMBULANCE is often written backwards on the front of ambulances.
items.explanation: Step 1: A driver in front sees the ambulance in the rear-view mirror. Step 2: The mirror flips the backwards word. Step 3: So the driver reads AMBULANCE the right way and can quickly make way.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning

items.question: In a code, MANGO is written as OCPIQ. How is APPLE written in that code?
items.explanation: Step 1: Compare: M→O, A→C, N→P, G→I, O→Q. Each letter moves 2 steps forward. Step 2: Apply to APPLE: A→C, P→R, P→R, L→N, E→G. Step 3: APPLE becomes CRRNG.
items.source: R.S. Aggarwal, A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning
